name: SQLiteData (StructuredQueries decoding over GRDB)
baseline: SwiftData (the README's stated replacement target); measured only against GRDB and SQLite.swift
verdict_reason: The README calls it a fast replacement for SwiftData, but its only numbers compare it with other SQLite wrappers, not with SwiftData or Core Data. Against those it is 2.2x faster than GRDB with manual decoding and 6.3x faster than GRDB with Codable, and about 6% slower than Lighter.
tier_reason: First-party numbers from a public suite with library versions, but no hardware, OS or build configuration stated.
claimed_speedup: SQLiteData 1.0.0: 8.511 vs 18.819 for GRDB 7.4.1 with manual decoding (2.2x, derived from page data) and 53.326 for GRDB with Codable (6.3x, derived from page data); Lighter 1.4.10 (8.059) and Enlighter-generated raw SQLite (7.183) are faster.
workload: Lighter's performance suite: load all ~16,000 rows of the Northwind Orders table into Swift values, repeated; total duration reported.
one_liner: SwiftData-style observation over SQLite; decodes rows 2.2x faster than GRDB's hand-written mapping, but has no published SwiftData numbers.
how_it_is_fast: Tables are declared with the StructuredQueries @Table macro, which generates a decoder that reads columns in order from the SQLite statement instead of going through Codable's keyed containers. GRDB underneath provides connections, transactions and change observation. Per-row cost ends up close to Lighter's generated bindings.
use_it_when: You want SwiftData-like @FetchAll and @FetchOne observation in SwiftUI with SQL control and value types
You already use GRDB and decode rows through Codable
You need CloudKit sync without adopting SwiftData
skip_it_when: You need a measured win over SwiftData or Core Data before switching: none is published
caveats: No SwiftData or Core Data measurements despite the replacement claim
Hardware, OS and build configuration are not stated
A single query shape (full scan of one table) taken from Lighter's suite
Benchmark date inferred from the release of the measured version (1.0.0, September 2025)
tradeoffs: Brings in GRDB plus several Point-Free packages (StructuredQueries, Sharing, Dependencies)
You write SQL schemas and migrations; no model inference as in SwiftData
Macro-based models add macro expansion to build time

evidence.quote: SQLiteData is a [fast](#performance), lightweight replacement for SwiftData
